title: SonyAIBORobotSurface1 validation of redundant-readout numerical robustness
research_question: Does three-head Q.ANT readout averaging reduce reference/Q.ANT logit error on a non-floor transfer dataset while retaining Q.ANT classification accuracy?
hypothesis: On the frozen SonyAIBORobotSurface1 adaptation from Exp013, redundant3 will have lower mean absolute reference/Q.ANT logit error than the single-head control and Q.ANT TEST accuracy no more than one percentage point lower.
rationale: Exp017 and Exp018 both showed lower logit MAE, higher mean Q.ANT accuracy, and lower accuracy variance with three-head averaging, but Exp018 falsified the broader disagreement-reduction criterion. Exp019 preregisters the narrower numerical-robustness signal on a dataset with more compatibility disagreements than GunPoint.

dataset.name: SonyAIBORobotSurface1
dataset.input_adaptation: deterministic center crop 70→64 (drop 3 samples from each end)

candidates.redundant3: three independently parameterized Q.ANT Fourier/KAN heads 64→2; arithmetic mean of logits in reference and Q.ANT inference

success_criteria: Supported if redundant3 mean absolute logit error is strictly lower than control and redundant3 mean Q.ANT accuracy >= control - 0.01.
secondary_non_gating_observation: Report disagreement count and Q.ANT accuracy standard deviation, but do not use them to redefine success.
promotion_rule: No automatic PNN-v1 promotion. A supported result establishes cross-dataset evidence for numerical-error reduction, not universal disagreement reduction.
hardware_boundary: Q.ANT CPU/software simulation only; no physical photonic hardware performance claim.
